results.proposal_summary: Nature for Health (N4H) Phase II Expression of Interest is a grant opportunity funded by Germany (BMUV/IKI) through the N4H Multi-Partner Trust Fund, offering up to USD 2,250,000 per proposal to support country-led, preventative One Health policies and investments in nature aimed at reducing pandemic risks through biodiversity protection and environmental health integration. The call was open exclusively to governments (including sub-national entities) and regional intergovernmental entities from OECD DAC ODA-eligible countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America, and other developing regions. The application window ran from 10 January 2025 to 7 April 2025, with selection completed in August 2025; Phase II partners have already been announced. The ILO is ineligible as the call explicitly excludes non-governmental entities and UN agencies are not listed as eligible applicants.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call focuses on biodiversity, One Health, and pandemic prevention at the nature-health interface, with no connection to ILO's core mandate on labour standards, employment, social protection, or decent work.

results.proposal_summary: This call, managed by Hungary's National Coordination Centre (NCC-HU) under the EU Digital Europe Programme (2021–2027), provides grants totalling EUR 2,000,000 to enhance the cybersecurity resilience of domestic Hungarian SMEs. Eligible applicants are micro, small and medium-sized enterprises with at least three closed financial years operating in sectors defined by Hungary's Cybersecurity Act. results.proposal_summary: The IKI Large Grants programme, funded by the German Federal Government through the International Climate Initiative (IKI), supports international climate action and biodiversity conservation through projects addressing climate change mitigation, adaptation, and biodiversity conservation. Eligible applicants include NGOs, universities, research institutions, international intergovernmental organisations (including UN agencies), development banks, German implementing organisations, and commercial enterprises — but only as part of a consortium of at least two organisations. Grants range from EUR 5 million to EUR 20 million per project for implementation periods of up to 8 years, with projects eligible in ODA-eligible countries worldwide. The call is currently closed; the most recent cycle was the ILG Call 2025. The selection process involves two phases: an outline phase (ideas competition) and an invitation-only proposal phase. At least 50% of IKI funding must be implemented by local organisations.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the IKI Large Grants explicitly includes UN organisations as eligible applicants and funds transformative projects in developing countries relevant to just transitions and sustainable development, the primary focus is climate change mitigation, adaptation, and biodiversity — only partially overlapping with ILO's core mandate of labour standards, employment, and social protection.

results.proposal_summary: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), through its Addis Ababa office, has launched a second Call for Proposals (II CfP - Primissima Emergenza) under initiative AID 013351/01/0, providing €280,000 for emergency humanitarian assistance to Sudanese populations affected by the ongoing armed conflict. The initiative is part of a broader €5,000,000 programme supporting lifesaving essential services and protection for vulnerable groups in Sudan.

results.proposal_summary: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), through its Dakar regional office, is launching a comparative selection procedure for the grant-based assignment of initiative AID 013406 'GUIMARÉ – Sostegno integrato alla risicoltura di mangrovia per la sicurezza alimentare, l'empowerment femminile e la resilienza climatica in Repubblica di Guinea' to be implemented in Guinea. The total funding is €3,000,000 (non-reimbursable). Eligible applicants are exclusively Civil Society Organisations (OSC) and other non-profit entities registered in the Italian OSC registry under Article 26(3) of Law 125/2014, which may participate individually or as a Temporary Association of Purpose (ATS). results.ilo_match_evidence: While the initiative touches on food security, women's empowerment, and climate resilience — areas tangentially related to ILO's decent work agenda — the call is restricted to Italian-registered civil society organisations and does not align with ILO's core mandate areas of labour standards, employment policy, social protection, or social dialogue.

results.proposal_summary: AICS (Italian Agency for Development Cooperation) launched this public comparative call on 30 September 2026 with a total budget of EUR 15,000,000 to finance synergistic initiatives proposed by Italian civil society organisations (OSCs) under the Technical Support Spending framework of the Global Fund for AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. The call supports programmes aligned with the Global Fund Strategy 2023–2028 aimed at ending the three epidemics and achieving Universal Health Coverage by 2030. Eligible applicants are exclusively OSCs and non-profit entities registered in the Italian national list under Law 125/2014, Article 26, or consortia (ATS) led by such organisations. Applications must be submitted via the SISTAKE platform by 12 January 2027. Co-financing is a structural element of the instrument, and applicants must have prior platform accreditation.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call focuses exclusively on global health programming (HIV/AIDS, TB, Malaria) through civil society organisations, which falls outside the ILO's core mandate areas of labour standards, employment, social protection, and decent work, and ILO is not an eligible applicant type.

results.proposal_summary: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), through its Ouagadougou office, issues an open call for proposals under the AgrEcoNUS+ programme (funded by the European Union under DeSIRA+ and AICS) to select a partner to implement the AgrEcoNUS+/LEAP action in Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire. The action aims to enhance agroecological NUS (Neglected and Underutilized crop Species) value chains and markets by supporting local economic actors — primarily MSMEs, cooperatives and associations — through business development, capacity building, marketing, financial support, and market partnership development, contributing to AgrEcoNUS+ Result 3. The maximum grant is EUR 2,700,000 (covering 100% of eligible costs) for a maximum action duration of 36 months. Eligible applicants are NGOs, CSOs, and other civil society/private-sector entities with technical, management and territorial capacities to operate in both countries; UN agencies and intergovernmental organisations are not among the eligible categories. The deadline for submission is 16 December 2026.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call focuses on agroecological value chain development and MSME/cooperative support in Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire, which is outside ILO's core mandate of labour standards, employment policy, social protection and decent work, though it has marginal linkages to rural employment and sustainable enterprises.

results.proposal_summary: This AFD (Agence Française de Développement) landing page describes multiple grant co-financing mechanisms for civil society organizations (CSOs) and NGOs implementing international solidarity and development projects. The primary mechanism, the CSO Initiatives Platform, co-finances projects of at least €300,000–€500,000 (up to 80–90% of total budget) in DAC-eligible countries, targeting French and local CSOs for capacity building, education for development, and solidarity initiatives. Additional mechanisms include the now-suspended FISONG facility (innovative thematic projects), APCC (crisis/post-crisis calls), and FSOF (feminist organizations support fund). All eligible applicant types are CSOs, NGOs, French associations, foundations, and non-profit organizations; UN agencies and intergovernmental organizations are not eligible. No currently open call with a future deadline is presented on this aggregator page, and the FISONG has been suspended since 2023.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While some FISONG themes (social protection, financial inclusion of migrants, vocational training) touch on ILO mandate areas, the entire financing framework is exclusively designed for CSOs/NGOs and does not include UN agencies or IGOs as eligible applicants, making it structurally incompatible with ILO participation.

results.proposal_summary: Switzerland's State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) launched its second call for proposals on 9 January 2026 to mobilise reconstruction projects in Ukraine in cooperation with Swiss companies, with the federal government contributing up to CHF 150 million (CHF 500 million total for Swiss private sector projects under the 2025–2028 country programme). The call targets Swiss companies operating in Ukraine and focuses on strengthening public infrastructure, including energy, housing, public transport, health, and humanitarian demining, with individual project funding ranging from CHF 3 million to CHF 30 million. A two-stage process involves initial idea submission followed by a full proposal for selected companies, with interviews to clarify outstanding questions; the deadline was 8 March 2026. Eligibility is restricted exclusively to Swiss companies, making UN agencies and the ILO ineligible.
